mainTopic: Weather and the danger of מילה, the מָשׁוּךְ and תרומה (רב הונא refuted), and the טומטום in the ברייתא
overview: The amud opens by finishing the question of why the Jewish people did not do מילה in the מדבר. One answer is that the healthy north wind did not blow for them, so מילה was dangerous. רב פפא learns from this that we do not do מילה or bloodletting on a cloudy day or a day of south wind. He adds that nowadays people rely on ״שומר פתאים ה׳״. A ברייתא adds that the north wind did blow every night at midnight, because midnight is an עת רצון. Next, רב הונא rules that by Torah law a מָשׁוּךְ may eat תרומה, but the רבנן decreed against him. The גמרא explains that a פסוק quoted for redoing his מילה is only an אסמכתא. In the end, a ברייתא that lets a מָשׁוּךְ eat תרומה refutes רב הונא. The גמרא then works through that ברייתא's rules about a טומטום, with אביי and רבא each explaining how a טומטום can have 'wives'. Finally, it begins comparing the מָשׁוּךְ question to a dispute of תנאים about who may be circumcised only by day, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Another reason they skipped מילה: no north wind
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a second answer for why the Jewish people did not do מילה in the מדבר: the north wind did not blow for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, say it was because the north wind did not blow for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another answer to the earlier question of why there was no מילה in the מדבר. The answer is that the north wind, which helps healing, never blew there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the cool, healthy north wind, a person recovering from מילה would be in danger. So skipping מילה was a matter of safety, not neglect. This is an alternative to the earlier answer given on the previous part of the daf.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces another possible answer
The north wind, seen as healthy and healing

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא נְשִׁיב לְהוּ רוּחַ צְפוֹנִית.
phrases.english: because the north wind did not blow for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question, from before this section, of why מילה was not done in the מדבר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative explanation based on danger to health
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think they had no good reason to hold off on מילה, or that the only reason was the earlier one.
steps.terutzMaskana: Without the north wind, מילה was medically dangerous, so they were exempt.

steps.title: A ברייתא proves the north wind did not blow
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports the claim that the north wind never blew during the forty years in the מדבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: All those forty years that the Jewish people were in the מדבר, the north wind did not blow for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up the answer it just gave. The ברייתא states that the north wind did not blow in the מדבר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 1 is not a guess. It rests on an older teaching that clearly says the north wind was missing all forty years.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא; introduces a supporting source

phrases.english: As it is taught: All those forty years
that Israel was in the wilderness,
the north wind did not blow for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides a source for the answer in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the north wind did not blow in the מדבר
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that the north wind did not blow for forty years

steps.title: Why was the north wind held back?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the north wind did not blow for the Jewish people in the מדבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up its next move: why was this healthy wind kept away from them? The answers come in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on the ברייתא. It is a request to understand the reason behind the fact the ברייתא reports.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ברייתא in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the north wind did not blow for the Jewish people in the מדבר

steps.title: Two reasons: they were under rebuke, or to protect the clouds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives two possible reasons. Either the people were under Divine rebuke, or the wind was held back so the ענני כבוד would not be scattered.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you wish, say it was because they were under rebuke. And if you wish, say it was so that the ענני כבוד would not be scattered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with two options for why the north wind did not blow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reason is a punishment: the people were נזופים, under rebuke, and did not deserve this good wind. The second reason is protective: a strong wind would have scattered the ענני כבוד that surrounded them.

keyTerms.meaning: Under rebuke or censure from ה׳
The Clouds of Glory that surrounded the Jewish people in the מדבר

phrases.english: If you wish, say: because they were under rebuke,
and if you wish, say:
so that the Clouds of Glory would not be scattered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either the people were under rebuke, or the wind was held back to protect the ענני כבוד.

steps.title: רב פפא: no מילה or bloodletting on a cloudy or south-wind day
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא draws a practical rule from this: on a cloudy day or a day when the south wind blows, we do not do מילה and we do not let blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Therefore, on a cloudy day or a day of south wind, we do not circumcise on it and we do not let blood on it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא turns the idea that weather affects healing into a practical rule for today.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the lack of a north wind made מילה dangerous in the מדבר, bad weather is a real health risk. So on a cloudy day or a day of south wind, we hold off on מילה and on bloodletting, which was a common medical treatment.
steps.whyThisMatters: This step shows the story about the מדבר being used for a real rule of safety: health risks can push off the timing of מילה.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Therefore,
a cloudy day and a day of south wind,
we do not circumcise on it,
and we do not let blood on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical rule from the idea in steps 1-2 that the weather affects the danger of מילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On a cloudy day or a day of south wind, we do not do מילה or bloodletting.

steps.title: Nowadays people rely on ה׳ protecting the simple
steps.stepSummary: Nowadays, since many people ignore this concern, we apply the פסוק ״שומר פתאים ה׳״‎, ה׳ protects the simple.
steps.simpleTranslation: But nowadays, when many people have trodden on it, ‘ה׳ guards the simple.’
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא himself adds a limit to his rule. Since most people today no longer worry about this danger, they may rely on ה׳'s protection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a risk is something that the public commonly ignores (דשו בה רבים), we say ה׳ watches over people who act simply. So people who do מילה or let blood on such days are not considered to be doing something forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Many people have trodden on it, meaning the public commonly does it

steps.whatToRemember: Weather can make מילה dangerous, which explains the מדבר and leads to רב פפא's rule. But where the public ignores a risk, we rely on ״שומר פתאים ה׳״.

phrases.english: But nowadays, when many have trodden on it,
phrases.notes: Literally 'trampled on it': so many people do it that it has become a normal path.

phrases.english: ‘ה׳ guards the simple.’

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רב פפא's rule for nowadays.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Nowadays, since the public commonly does this, we rely on ״שומר פתאים ה׳״.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the north wind blew every night at midnight
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that during the forty years in the מדבר, the north wind blew every single night at midnight, and it brings the פסוק about מכת בכורות at midnight.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: All those forty years that Israel was in the מדבר, there was no day on which the north wind did not blow at midnight, as it says: ‘And it was at midnight, and ה׳ struck every firstborn…’
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא saying the north wind did blow in the מדבר, but only at midnight. It supports this with the פסוק from יציאת מצרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a detail to the earlier ברייתא: the wind was missing during the day, but it came every night at midnight. The פסוק is quoted to link midnight to a special time, though how it proves this is not yet clear. The גמרא will ask about that next.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; introduces a ברייתא
As it is said; introduces a פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: This does not contradict step 2. The first ברייתא means the wind did not blow in a normal way, while this one says it came only at midnight. Since it came only at night, it was not enough to make מילה safe.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כׇּל אוֹתָן אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: All those forty years
that Israel was in the wilderness,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיָה יוֹם שֶׁלֹּא נָשְׁבָה בּוֹ
phrases.english: there was no day on which there did not blow
the north wind at midnight,
as it is said: ‘And it was at midnight,
and ה׳ struck every firstborn, etc.’

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a detail to the ברייתא of step 2: the north wind did come, but only at midnight.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every night in the מדבר, the north wind blew at midnight.

steps.title: How does the פסוק show this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a פסוק about מכת בכורות in מצרים teaches anything about the north wind in the מדבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the derivation?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the quoted פסוק proves the ברייתא's point, since the פסוק talks about מצרים and not about wind. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only says that something happened at midnight in מצרים. The connection to a nightly wind for forty years needs to be explained.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the learning, meaning how is this derived?

phrases.english: What is the derivation?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the פסוק in step 7 supports the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the פסוק about midnight in מצרים teaches that the north wind blew at midnight in the מדבר

steps.title: A time of Divine favor is something real
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק teaches that an עת רצון, a time of Divine favor, is significant. Midnight stayed a special time, so the healthy wind came then.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us that a time of favor is a real thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the link: midnight was a time of Divine favor at יציאת מצרים, and it kept that quality. That is why the good north wind came at midnight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק shows that midnight was the moment ה׳ acted to save the Jewish people. Because an עת רצון matters, even while they were under rebuke in the מדבר, that special moment still brought them the healthy wind.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a real, significant thing

steps.whatToRemember: In the מדבר, the north wind was held back, so מילה was not done. Yet it came every night at midnight, because midnight is an עת רצון, a time of Divine favor.

phrases.english: This teaches us
that a time of favor is a real thing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק teaches that an עת רצון is significant, so midnight remained a time of favor when the healthy wind blew.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Midnight, the moment of salvation in מצרים, stayed an עת רצון, so the north wind blew then.

steps.title: A מָשׁוּךְ may eat תרומה by Torah law
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that by Torah law a מָשׁוּךְ counts as circumcised and may eat תרומה. The רבנן made a גזירה against him because he looks like an ערל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: By Torah law, a man whose foreskin was drawn forward may eat תרומה. But the Sages decreed against him, because he looks like an uncircumcised man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ruling from רב הונא about a מָשׁוּךְ, a man who was circumcised but whose skin was later pulled forward to cover the area again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא splits the law into two levels. On the Torah level, the original מילה still counts, so a כהן in this state may eat תרומה. On the rabbinic level, the רבנן treat him like an ערל because of how he looks.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who was circumcised, but whose remaining skin was drawn forward to cover the area again
The holy portion of produce given to a כהן, which an ערל may not eat

steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of this section tests whether רב הונא is right that a מָשׁוּךְ is only a rabbinic problem and not a Torah problem.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
By Torah law, one whose foreskin was drawn forward
phrases.notes: He means a man who already had a proper מילה, but the leftover skin was later pulled forward to cover it.

phrases.english: may eat תרומה,
but from the words of the Sages, they decreed against him,
because he looks like an uncircumcised man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, separate from the discussion of the wind and the עת רצון in steps 7-9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By Torah law a מָשׁוּךְ is considered circumcised and may eat תרומה; the רבנן decreed otherwise because he looks like an ערל.

steps.title: A ברייתא says a מָשׁוּךְ needs מילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא from a ברייתא that says a מָשׁוּךְ must be circumcised again.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: One whose foreskin was drawn forward needs to be circumcised!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב הונא with a ברייתא that says a מָשׁוּךְ must be circumcised again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a מָשׁוּךְ must redo his מילה, it sounds like his first מילה does not count. That would mean he is an ערל even by Torah law, which goes against רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (usually from a ברייתא or משנה)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One whose foreskin was drawn forward needs to be circumcised!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's ruling from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that by Torah law a מָשׁוּךְ counts as circumcised.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he needs a new מילה, it looks like his old one does not count. Then he would be an ערל on the Torah level.

steps.title: The requirement is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא's requirement is מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא by saying the ברייתא is describing a rabbinic rule, not a Torah rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits exactly with what רב הונא already said: the רבנן decreed against a מָשׁוּךְ. So the ברייתא's 'needs to be circumcised' is that same rabbinic decree.

phrases.english: By rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reads the ברייתא as describing a rabbinic level of law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means a מָשׁוּךְ needs מילה by Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only means מדרבנן, which matches רב הונא.

steps.title: Why was this ever a challenge?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the questioner raised this ברייתא at all, since it only says 'needs' and never says it is Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who asked this, why did he ask it? It only teaches that he 'needs' it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wonders why anyone saw this ברייתא as a problem for רב הונא in the first place. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'needs' can easily mean a rabbinic need. So the challenge from step 11 seems weak from the start, and the גמרא wants to know what the questioner was thinking.

keyTerms.meaning: And the one who asked this question

phrases.english: And the one who asked it,
why did he ask it?
It only teaches that he 'needs'!
phrases.notes: The point is that 'needs' does not say whether it is Torah law or rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks back at the challenge of step 11 and asks why it was raised.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What made the questioner think the ברייתא was talking about Torah law?

steps.title: He was misled by the end of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The questioner was led astray by the later part of the ברייתא, which begins with רבי יהודה saying a מָשׁוּךְ should not be circumcised because it is dangerous.
steps.simpleTranslation: He erred because of the latter clause: רבי יהודה says, he should not be circumcised, because it is dangerous for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the questioner was looking at the end of the same ברייתא. That ending starts with רבי יהודה's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that a second מילה is too dangerous, so a מָשׁוּךְ should not do it. The other רבנן answer him in the next step, and their answer is what made the questioner think this is Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: He erred because of the latter clause

phrases.english: He erred because of the latter clause,
Rabbi Yehuda says:
He should not be circumcised,
because it is dangerous for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The questioner was misled by the end of the ברייתא, which begins with רבי יהודה's view that a second מילה is dangerous.

steps.title: The רבנן answer רבי יהודה with history and פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer that many people redid their מילה in the days of בן כוזיבא and still had children. They support the requirement with two פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: But didn't many get circumcised again in the days of בן כוזיבא, and they had sons and daughters? As it says, 'He must surely be circumcised,' even a hundred times. And it says: 'He has broken My covenant,' to include the one whose foreskin was drawn forward.
steps.whatsHappening: This is still inside the ברייתא. The רבנן reply to רבי יהודה that a second מילה is not dangerous, and they bring פסוקים showing it is required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First they prove from experience that it is safe: many people did it and still had children. Then they quote פסוקים from the תורה, and that is why the questioner thought a מָשׁוּךְ needs מילה by Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: The leader of a revolt against Rome (also known as בר כוכבא)
'He must surely be circumcised': the doubled word is read as 'even many times'

steps.whyThisMatters: These פסוקים are what made the question in step 11 look like a real challenge to רב הונא.

phrases.english: They said to him:
But didn't many get circumcised again
in the days of ben Koziva
and they fathered sons and daughters,
as it is said: 'He must surely be circumcised,'
even one hundred times,
and it says: 'He has broken My covenant'
to include the one whose foreskin was drawn forward.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: וַהֲלֹא הַרְבֵּה מָלוּ בִּימֵי בֶּן כּוֹזֵיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes quoting the end of the ברייתא, which is the source of the questioner's mistake from step 14.
steps.raayaObject: A מָשׁוּךְ must be circumcised again, and doing so is not dangerous.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The many people in the days of בן כוזיבא who did it and had children, plus the פסוקים 'הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל' and 'אֶת בְּרִיתִי הֵפַר'.

steps.title: Why bring a second פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed 'and it says' to bring a second פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the point of 'and it says'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא brought a second פסוק when it already had one. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל' already seemed to teach that a man can be circumcised again. So the extra פסוק 'אֶת בְּרִיתִי הֵפַר' looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it says': a phrase that brings an extra פסוק

phrases.english: What is 'and it says'?
phrases.notes: He means: why did the ברייתא need a second פסוק?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the two פסוקים quoted in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the ברייתא need two פסוקים for one law?

steps.title: The first פסוק could be about leftover shreds
steps.stepSummary: The first פסוק could have been read as only being about leftover shreds of skin that ruin a מילה. So the second פסוק is needed to teach about a מָשׁוּךְ.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say that this 'He must surely be circumcised' comes to include shreds of skin that hold back the מילה, come and hear: 'He has broken My covenant,' to include the one whose foreskin was drawn forward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that each פסוק has its own job, so the second one is not extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think 'הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל' only means: go back and cut any leftover shreds that make the מילה incomplete. So 'אֶת בְּרִיתִי הֵפַר' is needed to teach that a מָשׁוּךְ must also redo his מילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Shreds of skin left behind that make a מילה not count until they are removed

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: by Torah law a מָשׁוּךְ counts as circumcised, and the need to redo it is מדרבנן. The ברייתא's פסוקים confused the questioner. The גמרא shows that the second פסוק, 'אֶת בְּרִיתִי הֵפַר', is the one aimed at the מָשׁוּךְ.

phrases.english: And if you would say:
this 'He must surely be circumcised'
comes to include shreds of skin
that hold back the מילה,
phrases.notes: These are leftover bits of skin. Until they are cut, the מילה does not count.

phrases.english: come and hear: 'He has broken My covenant,'
to include the one whose foreskin was drawn forward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first פסוק might only cover leftover shreds, so the second פסוק is needed to include the מָשׁוּךְ.

steps.title: The verse was only a support, not the source
steps.stepSummary: The questioner thought the law was from the Torah because a פסוק was quoted. In truth it is rabbinic, and the פסוק is only a support.
steps.simpleTranslation: He thought that since the ברייתא brings a פסוק, the law must be from the Torah. But that is not so. It is only rabbinic, and the פסוק is just a support.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining why the questioner was confused. He saw a פסוק quoted and assumed the rule was Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Quoting a פסוק does not always mean the law comes from the Torah. Sometimes חז"ל make a rule and attach it to a פסוק as a hint, which is called an אסמכתא. So the requirement to redo the מילה of a מָשׁוּךְ stays rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: A mere support: a פסוק used as a hint for a rabbinic rule

steps.whatToRemember: A פסוק quoted in a ברייתא can be just an אסמכתא. The law itself can still be only rabbinic.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume every rule with a פסוק attached is Torah law. Here the גמרא says outright that it is not.

phrases.english: He thought: since [the ברייתא] brings for it
phrases.notes: 'He' is the one who raised the objection back in step 11.

phrases.english: a derivation (a verse), it must be Torah law.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets, 'a verse', and some don't. The meaning is the same either way.

phrases.english: But it is not so: it is rabbinic,
and the verse is a mere support.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא סָבַר: מִדְּקָא נָסֵיב לַהּ תַּלְמוּדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer from step 14 about why the questioner was misled.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did the questioner think this ברייתא shows Torah law?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because a פסוק was quoted. But the פסוק is only an אסמכתא, and the law is rabbinic.

steps.title: A ברייתא about who may eat תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא listing cases: טומטום, מָשׁוּךְ, one born circumcised, and אנדרוגינוס. It says which of them may eat תרומה and קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: A טומטום may not eat תרומה, but his wives and slaves may. A מָשׁוּךְ and one born circumcised may eat. An אנדרוגינוס may eat תרומה but not קדשים. A טומטום may eat neither תרומה nor קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to challenge רב הונא, who said a מָשׁוּךְ may not eat תרומה. Here the גמרא only quotes the source; the next step points out where the problem is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists several unusual bodily cases among כהנים. The key line for the challenge is that a מָשׁוּךְ may eat תרומה, which seems to go against רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection, usually from a ברייתא
A person whose genitals are hidden, so it is unknown if male or female
A person with both male and female features
The portion of produce given to כהנים
Sacrificial food, eaten only by male כהנים
Born already circumcised, without a foreskin

phrases.english: They raised an objection: a טומטום may not eat תרומה,
his wives and slaves may eat.
One whose foreskin was drawn forward, and one born circumcised:
these may eat.
An אנדרוגינוס may eat תרומה,
but may not eat sacrificial food.
A טומטום may not eat
neither תרומה nor sacrificial food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from explaining the earlier question to a new challenge against רב הונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that a מָשׁוּךְ may not eat תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא openly allows a מָשׁוּךְ to eat תרומה.

steps.title: The ברייתא lets a מָשׁוּךְ eat, against רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to the line that a מָשׁוּךְ may eat and says it refutes רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the ברייתא teaches: a מָשׁוּךְ and one born circumcised may eat. This is a refutation of רב הונא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא zooms in on the one line of the ברייתא that matters and says it refutes רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said a מָשׁוּךְ may not eat תרומה, at least by rabbinic law. The ברייתא says plainly that he may eat. So רב הונא's view clashes with a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, it teaches. Used to point to the key line of a source
The אמורא who said a מָשׁוּךְ may not eat תרומה

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches:
one whose foreskin was drawn forward, and one born circumcised:
these may eat,
a refutation of רב הונא!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points to the exact line in the ברייתא from step 19 that causes the problem.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He forbids what the ברייתא openly allows.

steps.title: רב הונא is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees: this is a real refutation of רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge. It has no answer for רב הונא, so his view is rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'תיובתא' a second time means the attack stands. The ruling stays as the ברייתא says: a מָשׁוּךְ may eat תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: A final refutation; the view cannot be defended

steps.whatToRemember: The ruling: a מָשׁוּךְ may eat תרומה. רב הונא's view is rejected.

phrases.english: It is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge from step 20.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב הונא is refuted. A מָשׁוּךְ may eat תרומה.

steps.title: How can a טומטום have wives?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא and asks how a טומטום could have wives at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: A טומטום may not eat תרומה, but his wives and slaves may. How does a טומטום have wives?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first line of the ברייתא and asks a clarifying question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טומטום has no visible male organ, and we are not sure if he is male. So how can the ברייתא talk about his 'wives' as if he were married?

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said; used to quote an earlier source again and look at it closely

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: טוּמְטוּם — אֵינוֹ אוֹכֵל בִּתְרוּמָה,
phrases.english: The Master said: a טומטום may not eat תרומה,
his wives and slaves may eat.
Wives for a טומטום, from where does he have them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא from step 19 to clarify its first line.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can a טומטום be married, so that the ברייתא can speak of his wives?

steps.title: Suggesting that he betrothed a woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the טומטום made קידושין. It brings a ברייתא that a טומטום's קידושין work, whether he betroths or is betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he betrothed a woman, as it is taught: a טומטום who betrothed, his קידושין are valid; if he was betrothed, his קידושין are valid...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts trying out an answer: maybe the 'wives' are women he betrothed. This is setting up the next move, and the next step challenges this suggestion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא says a טומטום can give קידושין, since he might be male. He can also receive קידושין, since he might be female. The word 'אילימא' shows this is only a suggestion, not yet the final answer.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say; brings a suggested answer that is about to be checked
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage

steps.confusionAlert: 'אילימא' means this is only a try. Don't treat it as the גמרא's final answer.

phrases.english: If you say that he betrothed [a woman],
as it is taught: a טומטום who betrothed [a woman],
his betrothal is a valid betrothal,
if he was betrothed [by a man], his betrothal is a valid betrothal,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first suggested answer to the question in step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Maybe the 'wives' are women he betrothed, since a טומטום's קידושין are valid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: טומטום שקידש קידושיו קידושין, נתקדש קידושיו קידושין

steps.title: His betrothal may only count to be strict, not to be lenient
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the last answer. A טומטום's קידושין may count only as a stringency, so they cannot be used to let his wife eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe the ברייתא only said his קידושין work to be strict. Do we also say they work to be lenient? He might be a woman, and a woman cannot betroth a woman!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the idea that the טומטום's wives are wives through קידושין. That קידושין might only count to be strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a ברייתא says the קידושין of a טומטום work, it may only mean we are worried he is a man, so the woman would need a גט. Letting her eat תרומה is a leniency, and we cannot rely on a doubtful marriage for that. He might be a woman, and then there is no marriage at all.

keyTerms.meaning: as a stringency, to be strict
as a leniency, to be lenient

steps.confusionAlert: A doubtful marriage can count to make things stricter, like needing a גט. That does not mean it counts to make things easier, like eating תרומה.

phrases.english: Say that he said it as a stringency;
phrases.notes: 'He' is the ברייתא from the last step, which said a טומטום's קידושין work.

phrases.english: do we say it as a leniency?
He is possibly a woman,
and a woman cannot betroth a woman!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דְּאָמַר לְחוּמְרָא, לְקוּלָּא מִי אָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 23, that the טומטום's wives come from valid קידושין.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא from step 23 explains how a טומטום has wives who eat תרומה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Doubtful קידושין only count to be strict. Eating תרומה is a leniency, so the doubt cannot support it.

steps.title: אביי: a טומטום whose testicles are visible
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the ברייתא is talking about a טומטום whose testicles can be seen from outside, so he is surely a male.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is talking about a case where his testicles are visible from the outside.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge. This טומטום is definitely a male, so his קידושין are fully valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge only worked because the טומטום might be a woman. If his testicles are visible, he is surely male, and only his organ is covered. His marriage is then certain, so his wife may eat תרומה.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
When his testicles are visible from the outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The טומטום might be a woman, so his קידושין are only doubtful.
steps.terutzMaskana: This טומטום is surely male, so his קידושין are certain and his wife eats תרומה.

steps.title: רבא: 'his women' means his mother
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different answer. The word נשיו in the ברייתא does not mean wives. It means his mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What does 'his women' mean? His mother.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the same problem another way. He reads the word in the ברייתא so it is not about wives at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא avoids the question of whether a טומטום can marry. He reads נשיו as 'his women', meaning his mother. A mother who was married to a כהן can eat תרומה through her כהן son.

phrases.english: Rava said:
What is 'his women'? His mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 24, different from אביי's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading a word in the ברייתא differently
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נשיו means wives, which needs valid קידושין.
steps.terutzMaskana: נשיו means his mother, so no קידושין are needed.

steps.title: Isn't it obvious that his mother eats?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's reading. Why would the ברייתא need to teach that his mother eats? That seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: His mother? That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבא's reading. It asks why the ברייתא would bother to teach something so simple.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who had a son with a כהן can eat תרומה because of him. So if נשיו means mother, the line seems to teach nothing new. A ברייתא should not state the obvious.

phrases.english: His mother? That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's reading in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading that נשיו means his mother.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ברייתא only says his mother eats, it teaches nothing new.

steps.title: Even a son who cannot have children lets his mother eat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the new point. We might think only a son who can have children lets his mother eat. The ברייתא teaches that even a טומטום does.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: one who can have children lets her eat, and one who cannot have children does not. So it teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'obvious' challenge. It shows what new thing the ברייתא teaches according to רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the ברייתא, we might think a son only lets his mother eat if he can have children himself. A טומטום cannot have children. The ברייתא teaches that he still lets his mother eat תרומה.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, a כהן's mother eats תרומה through him even if he cannot have children.

phrases.english: You might have said:
one who can have children lets her eat,
one who cannot have children does not let her eat,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: מוֹלִיד מַאֲכִיל, שֶׁאֵין מוֹלִיד אֵינוֹ מַאֲכִיל, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing what new point the text teaches (מהו דתימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a son who can have children lets his mother eat.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a son who cannot have children, like a טומטום, lets his mother eat.

steps.title: The ברייתא's repeated line fits אביי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the ברייתא's line that a טומטום does not eat תרומה or קדשים. That seems to repeat the first part, and it fits well with אביי: the first part means a surely male טומטום, and the later part means a doubtful one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a טומטום does not eat תרומה or קדשים. This fits אביי well. The first part taught about one who is surely an ערל, and the last part teaches about one who is possibly an ערל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a line from the ברייתא that supports אביי. It is setting up a problem for רבא, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא already said a טומטום does not eat, so why say it again? For אביי there are two different cases. The first is a טומטום who is surely male but cannot be circumcised, so he is surely an ערל. The later one is a fully covered טומטום, who is only possibly male and possibly an ערל. For רבא, who did not make this split, the repeat is harder to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: come and hear (a proof is coming)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A tumtum does not eat
neither teruma nor sacrificial food.
Granted, according to Abaye,
the first part taught one who is surely uncircumcised,
phrases.notes: This is the טומטום with visible testicles. He is surely male, but his organ is covered, so he cannot be circumcised.

phrases.english: and the last part teaches one who is possibly uncircumcised.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: טוּמְטוּם אֵינוֹ אוֹכֵל לֹא בִּתְרוּמָה וְלֹא בְּקָדָשִׁים. בִּשְׁלָמָא לְאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא of step 19 to test אביי's answer against רבא's.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's reading that the ברייתא speaks of a טומטום who is surely male.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The repeated line in the ברייתא, explained as two cases: surely an ערל, and possibly an ערל.

steps.title: How does רבא explain the second mention of a טומטום?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks that according to רבא, the later line about a טומטום in the ברייתא seems to be extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבא, why do I need the line about a טומטום at the end?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to רבא and asks why the ברייתא mentions a טומטום a second time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי explained the two lines as two different cases: a surely male טומטום and a doubtful one. רבא did not narrow the first line. For him it is about an ordinary, doubtful טומטום, and only the word נשיו means his mother. So for רבא, the later line saying a טומטום does not eat תרומה seems to repeat the first line.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part of a ברייתא or משנה
Why do I need it? (the line seems extra)
A person whose body is covered, so we cannot tell if he is male or female

phrases.english: But according to רבא,
why do I need the טומטום of the later part?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְרָבָא, טוּמְטוּם דְּסֵיפָא לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 29 showed the ברייתא fits אביי well. This step presses the same point against רבא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבא, the first line already rules that an ordinary, doubtful טומטום does not eat תרומה, so the later line about a טומטום looks like a pointless repeat.

steps.title: The later טומטום means a definite ערל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers for רבא that the later line is not about a טומטום at all but about a man who is surely uncircumcised.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'טומטום' mean here? A man who is uncircumcised.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבא: in the later line, the word טומטום really means an ערל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the later line is no longer a repeat. It teaches a separate rule about an uncircumcised man. But this answer will itself be questioned in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: What? (what does this word mean here)

phrases.english: What is 'טומטום'? An uncircumcised man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading a word in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The later line repeats the rule of a טומטום.
steps.terutzMaskana: The later line is about a definite ערל, so it is not a repeat.

steps.title: Why teach that a definite ערל cannot eat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks that if even a maybe-ערל cannot eat תרומה, it is obvious that a definite ערל cannot eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, if a man who is only maybe uncircumcised cannot eat, would a man who is surely uncircumcised be allowed to eat?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 31. Teaching that a definite ערל cannot eat seems useless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the ברייתא already says a טומטום, who is only a doubtful ערל, does not eat. So of course a definite ערל does not eat. The new reading seems to make the line obvious instead of extra, which is no better.

keyTerms.meaning: Now (if even this is true, then surely...)

phrases.english: Now, a maybe-uncircumcised man does not eat,
phrases.notes: The טומטום is the maybe-ערל. We aren't sure he is male, but if he is, his covered organ means he is uncircumcised.

phrases.english: so would a surely uncircumcised man eat?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא סְפֵק עָרֵל לָא אָכֵיל — וַדַּאי עָרֵל אָכֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the later טומטום means a definite ערל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: if a doubtful ערל cannot eat, a definite one surely cannot, so there is nothing to teach.

steps.title: The later line gives the reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the later line is not a new rule. It explains why a טומטום cannot eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is explaining the reason: why does a טומטום not eat תרומה? Because he may be uncircumcised, and an uncircumcised man eats neither תרומה nor קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the later line is giving the reason for the first rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is not adding a new law about a definite ערל. It explains that a טומטום is kept from תרומה because he might be an ערל, and an ערל may not eat תרומה or קדשים. So for רבא the line is neither extra nor obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: He is saying the reason (the line explains, it does not add a rule)
The portion of produce given to a כהן

steps.whatToRemember: For רבא, the later line of the ברייתא is only the reason for the first rule: a טומטום may be an ערל, and an ערל cannot eat תרומה or קדשים.

phrases.english: He is saying what the reason is:

phrases.aramaic: מָה טַעַם טוּמְטוּם אֵינוֹ אוֹכֵל בִּתְרוּמָה?
phrases.english: What is the reason a טומטום does not eat תרומה?
Because he is maybe uncircumcised,
and an uncircumcised man does not eat
neither תרומה nor קדשים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 32 and finishes defending רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the line as an explanation, not a new rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The later line adds a separate and obvious law about a definite ערל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The later line explains the reason behind the first rule.

steps.title: Suggesting the מָשׁוּךְ dispute matches a dispute of תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the earlier dispute about a מָשׁוּךְ is like a dispute between תנאים, and quotes a ברייתא that some people may only be circumcised during the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is like a dispute of תנאים: a מָשׁוּךְ, a convert who converted already circumcised, a child whose time passed, and all others who need circumcision, including one with two foreskins, are circumcised only during the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the question of the מָשׁוּךְ. It suggests that the question of whether a מָשׁוּךְ is an ערל by Torah law is the same as an older dispute between תנאים, and starts quoting that source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion says all these people, including a מָשׁוּךְ, may be circumcised only by day. The other side, which starts in the next step, will treat some of them differently. The גמרא wants to see if these opinions line up with whether a מָשׁוּךְ counts as a real ערל.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say it is like a dispute between תנאים
A man who was circumcised but whose skin was drawn forward to cover it
A child whose eighth day passed without circumcision

steps.confusionAlert: This is only a suggestion. The גמרא is setting up a comparison and will check whether it really holds.

phrases.english: Let us say it is like a dispute of תנאים:
one whose skin was drawn forward, (and one born circumcised),
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets and some do not.

phrases.english: and a convert who converted when already circumcised,
and a child whose time passed,
and all other people being circumcised,

phrases.aramaic: לְאֵיתוֹיֵי מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שְׁתֵּי עֲרָלוֹת —
phrases.english: which comes to include one who has two foreskins,
are circumcised only during the day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the טומטום discussion to link the earlier מָשׁוּךְ dispute to a תנאים dispute.
steps.raayaObject: The dispute about whether a מָשׁוּךְ counts as a real ערל
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about who may be circumcised only during the day

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בר שמעון begins his opposing view
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בר שמעון starts to give his view, beginning with circumcision done at its proper time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בר שמעון says: at its proper time...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא begins quoting the other side of the dispute. His words continue in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בר שמעון starts by talking about a circumcision done on the eighth day. He will separate that case from the others. The full contrast with the first opinion comes in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: At its proper time (the eighth day)
A תנא who argues on the first opinion here

phrases.english: רבי אלעזר בר שמעון says:
at its proper time,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: בִּזְמַנּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second opinion in the ברייתא quoted in step 34.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The view of רבי אלעזר בר שמעון begins with a circumcision done at its proper time. The rest of his ruling follows in the next lines.
